theDefect.summary: A wrong-state deliverable. The participant-facing text layer of this Pennsylvania Rule 790 family was Vermont's, borrowed from vt_seal_nonconviction-set.
theDefect.consequence: A participant following this packet would have been directed to the Vermont Superior Court, Criminal Division, on Vermont forms 200-00130, 200-00132 and 600-00228, for a Pennsylvania petition that is filed with a Pennsylvania Clerk of Courts.
theDefect.rootCause: scripts/build-census-v1-pa_pardon_expungement-set.mjs is a fork of the Vermont non-conviction builder. Confirmed by reading both: the fork's own header docblock is correct Pennsylvania (two routes, Pa.R.Crim.P. 790, 'WHY NO BOX IS MARKED ON EITHER FORM'), while the prose-emitting functions beneath it were carried over verbatim from Vermont. scripts/build-census-v1-vt_seal_nonconviction-set.mjs line 802 carries the identical 'File the completed packet with the **Vermont Superior Court, Criminal Division**' sentence.
theDefect.fixturesWereNotTheDefect: Both bound source PDFs are genuine Pennsylvania Rule 790 documents and rehash exactly against source-receipt.json. The defect was entirely in the text layer the builder emits.

contaminatedRecordsFound.howEnumerated: grep -rlE "Vermont|Superior Court|200-00130|200-00132|600-00228" over data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1/pa/, then a full read of every hit plus the builder, plus a decompressed-stream scan of the two delivered packet PDFs.

records.whatWasWrong: The 'Where you file this' section named the Vermont Superior Court, Criminal Division and its 'unit'; cited Vermont forms 200-00130, 200-00132 and 600-00228; described a Vermont State's Attorney stipulation route; declined to state fee or service on the ground that neither was established; falsely claimed a fee-waiver form was included in the packet; instructed the participant to answer a non-conviction question that appears on no Pennsylvania form and asserted the packet had already stated the participant was not convicted; described a third route this family does not have; and closed by calling the contents 'official Vermont forms'.
records.severity: participant-facing; the defect named in the assignment

records.whatWasWrong: Both counsel questions were Vermont questions put in front of counsel about a Pennsylvania family. The first asked counsel to confirm a marking of 'question 2 of 200-00130' across 'all three of this family's routes' — a form this family does not file, a marking it does not make, and a route count it does not have.
records.severity: would have consumed counsel review on a false premise; the assignment flagged this as mattering as much as the instructions

records.whatWasWrong: Three of five findings were Vermont: that the family 'files the same three forms as the Vermont sealing-by-conviction families'; that the census records THREE routes; that question 2 of 200-00130 is route-determined and the packet marks 'I was not convicted'; and that '600-00228 is a financial affidavit'.
The routeSelectionNote described marking question 2 of Vermont form 200-00130, and 14 refusal reasons attributed field ownership to 'the State's Attorney', a Vermont office.

contaminatedRecordsFound.aFifthProblemInsideTheFourth: The routeSelectionNote was not merely wrong-state, it was false about this packet's own contents: it claimed the packet marks 'I was not convicted for the offenses listed above', while routeSelectionsMade in the same file is an empty array and the builder marks no box on either form. That false claim is what generated the false counsel question in approval-request.json.
cleanRecordsConfirmed: The composed process_guidance page rendered into pages 3-5 of each packet PDF was already correct Pennsylvania — 'Clerk of Courts for the county', 'Pennsylvania State Police criminal history', two routes — and was not changed.
The two bound source PDFs, the per-document filled fixtures, source-receipt.json, build-status.json and reports/actual-writes.json carried no Vermont content.

replacements.to: Served on the Commonwealth — the District Attorney as attorney for the Commonwealth — which then has 60 days from service to consent, object or do nothing; the judge then grants, denies or schedules a hearing; if granted without Commonwealth consent the order is stayed 30 days pending appeal; keep proof of service.

aPreexistingDeterminismDefectIFixed.found: The first three rebuilds each produced a different canonical.pdf (47579a0a…, 699ec5dd…, 1e3cc102…). Byte-diffing two of them showed exactly 6 differing bytes, in /CreationDate and /ModDate: 'D:20260902014410Z' versus 'D:20260902014625Z'.
aPreexistingDeterminismDefectIFixed.cause: The assembled packet PDFDocument was created without a pinned date, so it carried a wall-clock timestamp. renderComposedPdf already pins the builder's own FIXED_DATE for exactly this reason; the packet assembly did not.
aPreexistingDeterminismDefectIFixed.notCausedByMyRepair: Demonstrated: the three divergent hashes were all produced AFTER my text repair was complete, and they differ from each other. The baseline fixture bytes were therefore never reproducible either.
aPreexistingDeterminismDefectIFixed.fix: Applied the builder's existing FIXED_DATE convention to the assembled packet, with a comment saying why. This changes no participant-facing content and no rendered pixel; it makes the fixture SHA-256 that the central raster receipt is keyed to reproducible.
aPreexistingDeterminismDefectIFixed.captainShouldNote: Other census-v1 builders may carry the same pattern. I checked only this one.
